raw_response:
I would keep my farm centered on the `cabbage-maize-cabbage` rotation, because on my land that is the most dependable way to use the full year and make good use of my well irrigation. I would put 3 mu into that core rotation, starting with spring cabbage, then summer maize on the same land, then autumn cabbage again. I would keep the other 3 mu for diversification: 1 mu chili for cash income, 1 mu kidney bean because it is easier on fertilizer and spreads risk, and 1 mu spinach because it fits well into the cooler part of the year and gives me a quick crop. Since I am experienced and educated, I would use mostly hybrid or improved seed, keep fertilizer relatively precise instead of excessive, irrigate on schedule rather than waiting for stress, and use pesticides only as much as needed to protect yield. I would put the highest inputs into cabbage, moderate inputs into chili and maize, low nitrogen into kidney bean, and a shorter, efficient program into spinach.
